cards.claim: An Auto Scaling group is a Regional construct: it can span Availability Zones, but not Regions.
links: [can span Availability Zones, but not AWS regions](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-regional-spans-azs-not-regions)

cards.claim: Data is not automatically copied from existing instances to new instances the group launches; use lifecycle hooks to copy data, or an Amazon RDS database with replicas.
If you delete an Auto Scaling group that has running instances, the instances are terminated and the group is deleted.
A group can have only one launch configuration at a time, and a launch configuration cannot be modified after it is created; to change it, create a new launch configuration and update the group.
You do not have to use ELB to use Auto Scaling: the EC2 health check can identify and replace unhealthy instances on its own.

A single Auto Scaling group can provision and scale EC2 capacity across different instance types, Availability Zones, and On-Demand, RI and Spot purchase options, with a chosen split between On-Demand and Spot capacity.
EC2 Auto Scaling cannot scale past the EC2 limit on the number of instances the account can run; to get more, submit an EC2 instance limit request.
Creating an Auto Scaling group from an existing instance does not create a new AMI.
cards.scope: per Auto Scaling group created from an existing instance.

cards.claim: A predictive scaling policy brings a prediction algorithm similar to the one offered through an AWS Auto Scaling plan into EC2 Auto Scaling as a native scaling policy, so you do not have to create a scaling plan just to use predictive scaling.

EC2 Auto Scaling does not automatically add a volume when an existing volume approaches capacity; a volume is attached to a new instance when that instance is added, and the EC2 API adds a volume to an existing instance.

NASA JPL processes about 4.4 TB of downlinked satellite data a day into up to 70 TB of data products on automatic scaling fleets: Spot Instances for the fault-tolerant processing and On-Demand with Capacity Reservations for critical processing.
